body.translated_text: <s>Samāsa Sūtra</s> — The <s>Sarvopakāriṇī</s> (Benefiting All) Commentary.

children.text: yadvāgvibhūtiramalākhilatattvajātānnānādya tattvamamalaṃ paribodhayantī /
children.translated_text: Whose splendor of speech, stainless, arising from all the categories of reality, illuminating the supreme pure reality in various ways,

children.text: śreyaḥ karoti jagatāṃ bhagavantamādyaṃ taṃ śrīmaharṣikapilaṃ prabhumānato 'smi // 1 //
children.translated_text: bestows well-being upon the worlds — I bow to that primordial <s>Bhagavān</s>, the glorious great sage <s>Kapila</s>. || 1 ||

children.text: uddidhīrṣustadunnītasūtratattvārthabuddhaye /
children.translated_text: Wishing to uplift [beings], for the understanding of the true meaning of the <s>sūtras</s> elucidated by him,

children.text: sarvopakāriṇīṃ kurve ṭīkāṃ guṇavaśaṃvadaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: I, obedient to [his] virtues, compose this commentary (<s>ṭīkā</s>) called <s>Sarvopakāriṇī</s>. || 2 ||

body.text:
athātrānādikleśakarmavāsanāsamudranipatitānanāthadīnānuddidhīrṣuḥ paramakṛpāluḥ svataḥsiddhatattvajñāno maharṣirbhagavān kapilo dvāviṃśatisūtrāṇyupādikṣat /
sūcanāt sūtramiti hi vyutpattiḥ /
tata etaiḥ samastatattvānāṃ sakalaṣaṣṭitantrārthānāṃ ca sūcanaṃ bhavati /
itaścedaṃ sakalasāṃkhyatīrthamūlabhūtaṃ tīrthāntarāṇi caitatprapañcabhūtānyeva /
sūtraṣaḍadhyāyī tu vaiśvānarāvatāramaharṣibhagavatkapilapraṇītā iyaṃ tu dvāviṃśatisūtrī tasyā api bījabhūtā nārāyaṇāvatāramaharṣibhagavatkapilapraṇīteti vṛddhāḥ /
tatrādau prathamasūtratrayeṇa sakalaprapañcamūlabhūtāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni sūcayati /
body.translated_text: Now, here, wishing to uplift those who are helpless, wretched, and have fallen into the ocean of beginningless afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), <s>karma</s>, and latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), the supremely compassionate great sage <s>Bhagavān Kapila</s>, whose knowledge of reality is self-established, taught twenty-two <s>sūtras</s>. The etymology of '<s>sūtra</s>' is 'that which indicates' (<s>sūcanāt</s>). Therefore, by these [sūtras], all the categories of reality and the entire content of the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> (Treatise of Sixty Topics) are indicated. Furthermore, this is the root-source of the entire <s>Sāṃkhya</s> tradition, and the other branches of the tradition are merely elaborations of this. The elders say that the <s>Sūtra-Ṣaḍadhyāyī</s> (Six-Chapter Sūtra Work) was composed by the great sage <s>Bhagavān Kapila</s> [who was] an incarnation of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, while this twenty-two-sūtra [work] — which is the seed even of that — was composed by the great sage <s>Bhagavān Kapila</s> [who was] an incarnation of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Therein, at the beginning, by means of the first three <s>sūtras</s>, the twenty-five categories of reality (<s>tattvas</s>), which are the root of the entire manifest world, are indicated.
[Sūtra 1:] The <s>prakṛtis</s> (primal natures) are eight. ||
[Sūtra 2:] The modifications (<s>vikāras</s>) are sixteen. ||
[Sūtra 3:] <s>Puruṣa</s> (the spirit). ||

body.text:
ayamarthaḥ sāṃkhyasiddhānte pañcaviṃśatistattvāni /
tatra mūlaprakṛtiḥ mahattattvam ahaṅkāraḥ śabdatanmātrā sparśatanmātrā rūpatanmātrā rasatanmātrā gandhatanmātrā cetyaṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ santi /
atra tattvāntarārambhakatvaṃ prakṛtitvam ataśca mahadādīnāṃ saptānāṃ pūrvapūrvavikṛtitve 'pi na atiḥ lakṣaṇasamanvayāt /
pañca buddhīndriyāṇi pañca karmendriyāṇi manaḥ gaganapavanajvalanasaliladharaṇyākhyāni pañca bhūtāni caitāni ṣoḍaśa vikārāḥ vikṛtaya eva na tattvāntārārambhakāṇi sarvaṃ vākyaṃ sāvadhāraṇamiti nyāyāt /
puruṣaḥ pañcaviṃśatitamaṃ tattvam /
ayaṃ ca na prakṛtirna vikṛtiḥ tābhyaḥ pṛthakkṛtya nirūpaṇāt /
anena jaḍatvapariṇāmitvakartṛtvādidharmavadbhyaḥ prakṛtyādibhyaḥ puruṣasya vailakṣaṇyamapi sūcitaṃ bhavati tathā ca kārikā /
body.translated_text: The meaning is this: In the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system, there are twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (categories of reality). Among them, the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> are: <s>Mūlaprakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>Mahattattva</s> (the Great Principle, i.e., intellect), <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — namely, the <s>śabda-tanmātra</s> (sound-subtle-element), <s>sparśa-tanmātra</s> (touch-subtle-element), <s>rūpa-tanmātra</s> (form-subtle-element), <s>rasa-tanmātra</s> (taste-subtle-element), and <s>gandha-tanmātra</s> (smell-subtle-element). Here, the characteristic of being a <s>prakṛti</s> is the capacity to originate another category; therefore, even though <s>Mahat</s> and the other seven are modifications of their respective prior [categories], there is no contradiction — due to the consistency of the defining characteristic. The sixteen modifications (<s>vikāras</s>) are: the five cognitive sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>), the five action-organs (<s>karmendriya</s>), the mind (<s>manas</s>), and the five gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) called space (<s>gagana</s>), wind (<s>pavana</s>), fire (<s>jvalana</s>), water (<s>salila</s>), and earth (<s>dharaṇī</s>) — these sixteen are modifications only, not originators of further categories, because the entire statement is to be understood as exclusive. <s>Puruṣa</s> is the twenty-fifth category. It is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s> (modification), since it is described separately from both. By this, the distinctiveness of <s>Puruṣa</s> from <s>Prakṛti</s> and the rest, which possess properties such as insentience (<s>jaḍatva</s>), capacity for transformation (<s>pariṇāmitva</s>), and agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>), is also indicated. And thus the <s>kārikā</s> [states]:

children.text: mūlaprakṛtiravikṛtirmahadādyāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ sapta /
children.translated_text: <s>Mūlaprakṛti</s> (root-nature) is unmodified; the seven beginning with <s>Mahat</s> are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and modifications;

children.text: ṣoḍaśakastu vikāro na prakṛtirna vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: the group of sixteen are modifications only; <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor modification.

body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: nanvetebhyo 'tiriktā anye 'pi bahavo ghaṭapaṭādayaḥ padārthā dṛśyante tatkathameṣāmupapattirata āha /
body.translated_text: Objection: But beyond these, many other entities such as pots, cloths, etc. are also seen. Then how is their existence accounted for? To this he says:
[Sūtra 4:] The operation of the three <s>guṇas</s> (<s>traiguṇyasañcāra</s>). ||

children.text: triguṇa eva traiguṇyaṃ sattvarajastamāṃsi teṣāṃ sañcāraḥ mattakapotakaṇṭhanyāyena pratikṣaṇaṃ vilakṣaṇapariṇāmo varttata iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which possesses the three <s>guṇas</s> is <s>traiguṇya</s>; [the three <s>guṇas</s> are] <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. Their <s>sañcāra</s> (operation) means that transformation into ever-differing forms occurs at every moment, according to the maxim of the neck of a drunken pigeon — this is what is to be supplied.

children.text: anena mūlaprakṛtistriguṇātmikā tritvena ca bhedabodhakena guṇāḥ parasparaviruddhasvabhāvāḥ prītyaprītiviṣādātmakāḥ sañcāreṇa ca saṅgatasamyakcaraṇārthakena teṣāṃ nityasabhāvaḥ puruṣārthe jananīye kāryānusāreṇa parasparasahāyatā ca /
children.translated_text: By this [sūtra], <s>Mūlaprakṛti</s> is constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>; and by the word 'three' which indicates distinction, the <s>guṇas</s> are of mutually opposed natures — characterized as pleasure (<s>prīti</s>), displeasure (<s>aprīti</s>), and stupefaction (<s>viṣāda</s>); and by [the word] <s>sañcāra</s>, meaning 'moving together properly,' their eternal co-existence is [indicated], as well as their mutual cooperation in accordance with the effects to be produced for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tataśca prakṛtermahadādīnāṃ bhūtebhyaśca ghaṭapaṭādisakalapadārthānāṃ triguṇalakṣaṇapariṇāmādeva saṃsiddhiḥ kāryotpādaśca nāpūrvaḥ kintvāvirbhāvamātraṃ sūkṣmakāraṇarūpeṇa sthitasya sthūlakāryakṣamarūpeṇa vipariṇāma iti sadvyāptivādaśca ityete siddhāntāḥ saṃsūcitā bhavantīti bodhyam //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the complete accomplishment of all entities — from <s>Prakṛti</s> through <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, and from the gross elements through pots, cloths, and all other objects — is solely through transformation characterized by the three <s>guṇas</s>. And the production of effects is not something entirely new; rather, it is merely a manifestation — a transformation of what already existed in its subtle causal form into a gross effect-form. Thus the doctrine of <s>sadvyāptivāda</s> (the theory of the pervasion of the existent, i.e., <s>satkāryavāda</s>) and these other doctrines are indicated — this should be understood.

body.text: nanu guṇānāmanavaratapariṇatisvabhāvatvāt kadācidapi dṛśyajātādarśanaṃ na syāt tataśca pralayocchedaḥ syādata āha /
body.translated_text: Objection: Since the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> is unceasing transformation, there should never be a non-manifestation of the visible world; and consequently, dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) would be an absolute annihilation. To this he says:
[Sūtra 5:] Involution (<s>pratisañcara</s>). ||

children.text: yathā sṛṣṭiprakriyānirvāhakastriguṇapariṇamastathā pratisañcāraḥ pratikūlopi vipariṇāmosti tathā ca pratilomapariṇāmena tattatkāryāṇāṃ svasvakāraṇe laye jāte triguṇāyāḥ prakṛteḥ sāmyasthitireva pralaya iti sūcitam /
children.translated_text: Just as the transformation of the three <s>guṇas</s> brings about the process of creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), so too there is a reverse transformation, called <s>pratisañcāra</s> (involution). Thus, through reverse-order transformation, when respective effects dissolve into their respective causes, the state of equilibrium of <s>Prakṛti</s>, constituted of three <s>guṇas</s>, is itself dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) — this is what is indicated.

children.text: tadā ca samānapariṇāmatvena vailakṣaṇyānāvirbhāva iti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: And then, due to their having an identical state of transformation, there is no manifestation of distinction — this is the meaning. //

body.translated_text: Now, in order to state the threefold classification for the purpose of distinguishing between the pleasure, pain, etc. that arise [for the self], he first states the internal [kind] with one [<s>sūtra</s>]:
The subjective (<s>adhyātma</s>). || 6 ||

children.text: ātmānamadhikṛtyetyadhyātmam taddvividhaṃ śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ceti śārīraṃ vātapittaśleṣmavaiṣamyanimittaṃ mānasaṃ kāmakrodhalobhamoherṣyāviṣayaviśeṣadarśanādarśananimittam /
children.translated_text: <s>Adhyātma</s> means 'pertaining to the self' (<s>ātmānam adhikṛtya</s>). It is of two kinds: bodily (<s>śārīra</s>) and mental (<s>mānasa</s>). The bodily [suffering] is caused by the imbalance of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm). The mental [suffering] is caused by the seeing or not-seeing of specific objects of desire (<s>kāma</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), greed (<s>lobha</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), and envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>).

children.text: etadubhayamapi āntaropāyasādhyatvādadhyātmamityucyate //
children.translated_text: Both of these are called <s>adhyātma</s> because they are remediable by internal means. //

body.translated_text: He states the two external divisions with two [<s>sūtras</s>]:
The objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>). || 7 ||
Pertaining to the elemental beings (<s>bhūta</s>) — humans, animals, birds, reptiles, plants, and the like — that is what is meant by <s>adhibhūta</s>. //
The divine (<s>ādhidaiva</s>). || 8 ||

children.text: yakṣarākṣasavināyakagrahādyāveśanimittametat /
children.translated_text: This is caused by the possession (<s>āveśa</s>) of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Vināyaka</s>-spirits, planetary influences (<s>graha</s>), and the like.

children.text: idaṃ dvayamapi bāhyopāyasādhyatvādbāhyamityuktam //
children.translated_text: This twofold [division] too is called external because it is remediable by external means. //

body.text: nanu satsvapi vilakṣaṇeṣu bahuṣu padārtheṣu puruṣasya tatsambandhābhāvāt kathaṃ tato duḥkhamatastatsāmagrīṃ nirūpayiṣurādau buddhīndriyāṇyāha /
body.translated_text: Now, even though there are many distinct objects in existence, since <s>puruṣa</s> (the conscious self) has no relation with them [by itself], how can suffering arise from them? Thus, intending to determine the aggregate [of factors enabling that relation], he first states the cognitive sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>):
Five are the <s>abhibuddhis</s> (intellectual faculties). || 9 ||

body.text: abhito buddhyante jñāyante vastūnyābhirityabhibuddhayaḥ buddhīndriyāṇi cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇarasanatvagākhyāni rūpaśabdagandharasasparśabodhakāni //
body.translated_text: Those by which objects are cognized from all sides (<s>abhitaḥ</s>) are the <s>abhibuddhis</s> — the cognitive sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>), named eye (<s>cakṣus</s>), ear (<s>śrotra</s>), nose (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), tongue (<s>rasana</s>), and skin (<s>tvak</s>), which are the revealers of form (<s>rūpa</s>), sound (<s>śabda</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), and touch (<s>sparśa</s>) [respectively]. //

body.text: anena ca jñānadvārā yogaṃ darśayituṃ karmendriyāṇyāha /
body.translated_text: And thereby, to show the connection [of puruṣa with objects] through the door of action, he states the organs of action (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>):
Five are the <s>karmayonis</s> (sources of action). || 10 ||

children.text: pañca indriyāṇi karmayonayaḥ karmaṇāṃ vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandānāṃ yonayaḥ kāraṇāni tāni ca vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthākhyāni /
children.translated_text: The five organs that are the <s>karmayonis</s> — the sources, i.e., causes, of actions such as speaking, grasping, moving, excreting, and rejoicing — are those called voice (<s>vāk</s>), hands (<s>pāṇi</s>), feet (<s>pāda</s>), anus (<s>pāyu</s>), and genitals (<s>upastha</s>).

children.text: anena karmaṇā tattadviṣayasānnidhyena tattatsambandhaḥ sūcitaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the relation [of puruṣa] with the respective objects through their proximity [brought about] by action is indicated. //

body.text: atha mahadahaṅkāramanasāmadhyavasāyābhimānasaṅkalpā asādhāraṇyo vṛttayaḥ tābhirvinendriyadvārā viṣayagrahāsambhavāt taistadgrahoktyā tāsāṃ nirūpitaprāyatvena tatsādhāraṇī vṛttirāha /
body.translated_text: Now, the distinctive functions of <s>mahat</s> (the great principle), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind) — namely, determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), self-attribution (<s>abhimāna</s>), and volition (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) — [being unique to each], apprehension of objects without [these] through the door of the senses alone is impossible. Since those [functions] are already mostly determined by their statement through [the description of] the sense-organs' apprehension of objects, he states their common function:
Five are the <s>vāyus</s> (vital breaths). || 11 ||

children.text: pañcasaṃkhyākāḥ prāṇāpānasamānodānavyānākhyāḥ vāyavaḥ mahadahaṅkāramanasāṃ sādhāraṇavṛttayaḥ jīvanasādhanāni /
children.translated_text: The five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>), called <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s>, are the common functions of <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>, and are the means of sustaining life.

children.text: tatra prāṇo nāsāgrahṛnnābhipādāṅguṣṭhavṛttiḥ apānaḥ kṛkāṭikāpṛṣṭhapāyupārśvopasthavṛttiḥ samāno hṛnnābhisarvasandhivṛttiḥ udāno hṛtkaṇṭhatālumūrddhabhrūmadhyavṛttiḥ vyānastvavṛttiriti //
children.translated_text: Among these: <s>prāṇa</s> operates at the tip of the nose, the heart, the navel, and the big toes; <s>apāna</s> operates at the back of the neck, the spine, the anus, the sides, and the genitals; <s>samāna</s> operates at the heart, the navel, and all the joints; <s>udāna</s> operates at the heart, the throat, the palate, the crown of the head, and the space between the eyebrows; and <s>vyāna</s> pervades everywhere. //

body.translated_text: He states the utility of the five [vital breaths]:
Five are the <s>karmātmans</s> (action-selves). || 12 ||

body.text: bhuktapītāhārajalāderasarudhirādeśca yathāyathaṃ prāpaṇameṣāṃ karma tadekānumeyatvena tatsvarūpātmakatā (?) ityarthaḥ // 12 //
body.translated_text: The proper distribution of eaten and drunk food, water, and the like, and of chyle (<s>rasa</s>), blood (<s>rudhira</s>), and so forth — this is their function; and since they are inferred solely through that [function], their essential nature consists in that — this is the meaning. // 12 //

body.text: nanvastu jñānakriyādvārā mahadabhimānasarvasaṅkalpānāṃ viṣayayogitvaṃ puruṣasya svapariṇāmitayā tanna ghaṭate ityāśaṅkāṃ vinivartayiṣurāha /
body.translated_text: Now, [one might object:] through the doors of cognition and action, <s>mahat</s> (determination), <s>abhimāna</s> (self-attribution), and all <s>saṅkalpas</s> (volitions) attain connection with objects — but since <s>puruṣa</s> is of unchanging nature, that [connection] is not possible for it. To remove this doubt, he states:
Fivefold <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). || 13 ||

children.text: anātmasvātmakhyātiravidyā sā ca vidyāvirodhinī pañcaparvā bhavati tāni ca parvāṇi avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśākhyāni /
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the cognition of the self in what is not the self (<s>anātma</s>). It is opposed to knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and has five divisions. Those divisions are called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life).

children.text: tathā ca yadavidyayā viparyayeṇāvadhāryate vastu asmitādayastatsvabhāvāstadabhiniviśante tataścātmano vivekena tatsambandha iti bhāvaḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: And thus: when an object is apprehended through <s>avidyā</s>, through error (<s>viparyaya</s>), then <s>asmitā</s> and the rest, which are of that [erroneous] nature, become attached to it. And thereby, through [the lack of] discrimination (<s>viveka</s>), the self becomes related to that [object] — this is the meaning. // 13 //

body.text: pañcāśadbhedeśu pratyayasargeṣu pañcaviparyayā nirūpitāḥ adhunā viśiṣṭeṣvaṣṭāviṃśatimaśaktimāha /
body.translated_text: Among the fifty divisions of the intellectual creation (<s>pratyayasarga</s>), the five errors (<s>viparyaya</s>) have been determined. Now he states the twenty-eight-fold incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>) among the distinguished [categories]:
Incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>) is of twenty-eight kinds. || 14 ||

body.text: indriyavadhā ekādaśa vuddhivadhāśca saptadaśa ityetāḥ aśaktaya ucyante /

children.text: indriyavadhā yathā /
children.translated_text: The impairments of the sense-organs are as follows:

children.text: bādhiryaṃ kuṣṭhatā 'ndhatvaṃ jaḍatā 'jighratā tathā /
children.translated_text: Deafness, leprosy, blindness, dullness, anosmia,

children.text: mūkatākauṇyapaṅgutvaklaibyodāvartamandatāḥ /
children.translated_text: muteness, crippled hands, lameness, impotence, constipation, and slowness.

children.text: iti buddhivadhāstu navatuṣṭīnāmaṣṭasiddhīnāṃ ca viparyayādbhavanti taditthaṃ jātā aśaktayo 'ṣṭāviṃśatidheti // 14 //
children.translated_text: The impairments of the intellect arise from the reversal of the nine <s>tuṣṭis</s> (contentments) and the eight <s>siddhis</s> (attainments). Thus produced, the incapacities are twenty-eight-fold. // 14 //

body.translated_text: The eleven impairments of the sense-organs (<s>indriyavadha</s>) and the seventeen impairments of the intellect (<s>buddhivadha</s>) — these are called the incapacities (<s>aśakti</s>).
Since [the topics of] <s>tuṣṭi</s> and <s>siddhi</s> have been introduced, he states them with two [<s>sūtras</s>]:
<s>Tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is ninefold. || 15 ||

children.text: yathoktam /
children.translated_text: As stated:

children.text: ādhyātmikyaścatasraḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The four internal [contentments] are named <s>prakṛti</s> (nature), <s>upādāna</s> (means), <s>kāla</s> (time), and <s>bhāgya</s> (fate).

children.text: bāhyāḥ viṣayoparamāt pañca nava tuṣṭayobhihitāḥ //
children.translated_text: The five external [contentments arise] from the cessation of [attachment to] sense-objects. Thus nine <s>tuṣṭis</s> are declared. //

body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
asyārthaḥ vivekasākṣātkāro hi prakṛtipariṇāmabhedaḥ taṃ ca saiva karotīti kṛtaṃ dhyānābhyāseneti kenacidupadiṣṭe tatra tuṣṭiḥ prakṛtyākhyā 1, atha prakṛteḥ sarvān pratyaviśeṣānna kevalaṃ tata eva vivekasākṣātkāraḥ kintu pravrajyayetyupadiṣṭe tuṣṭirupādānākhyā 2, pravrajyāpi kālaviśeṣaṇādareṇaiva vivekaṃ janayatyalamuttaptatayā ityupadiṣṭe tuṣṭiḥ kālākhyā 3, bhāgyenaiva vivekakhyātiriti tuṣṭirbhāgyākhyā 4, ityetāścatasraḥ prakṛtivyatiriktamātmānamadhikṛtya jāyanta ityādhyātmikya ucyante /
viṣayāḥ śabdasparśarūparasagandhākhyāḥ pañca teṣu arjanarakṣaṇakṣayabhogahiṃsādoṣadarśanaṃ tata uparamā viratayopi pañca te ca mahadahaṅkārādīnanātmana ātmanobhimanyamānasya vairāgye satyutpadyante 'to bāhyā ucyante /
imāśca nava uktaviparyayāḥ 5 aśaktibhiḥ 28 saha dvicatvāriṃśat 42 siddhiparipanthitvāddheyāḥ // ?// 15 //
body.translated_text: The meaning of this [is as follows]: The direct realization of discrimination (<s>vivekasākṣātkāra</s>) is indeed a modification of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), and she alone brings it about — when someone instructs that 'it is accomplished through the practice of meditation,' the satisfaction [born from that instruction] is called <s>Prakṛti</s> (the first, 'Nature') [satisfaction]. Then, [if instructed that] since <s>Prakṛti</s> is not distinguished with respect to all [individuals], the direct realization of discrimination comes not merely from that [meditation alone] but through renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>), the satisfaction is called <s>Upādāna</s> (the second, 'Means'). [If instructed that] renunciation too generates discrimination only through regard for a particular time, [since one is] sufficiently tormented — the satisfaction is called <s>Kāla</s> (the third, 'Time'). [The view that] the manifestation of discrimination comes through destiny (<s>bhāgya</s>) alone is the satisfaction called <s>Bhāgya</s> (the fourth, 'Fortune'). These four arise with reference to the self as distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s>, and therefore are called 'internal' (<s>ādhyātmika</s>). The objects — named sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — are five. Seeing the defects of acquisition, preservation, loss, enjoyment, and injury regarding them, the cessation [of desire] — the five abstentions (<s>virati</s>) — [arises]. These arise when dispassion is present in one who falsely identifies the non-self, such as <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), etc., as the self — therefore they are called 'external' (<s>bāhya</s>). These nine, being the opposites of [what has been] stated, together with the twenty-eight incapacities (<s>aśakti</s>), [form] forty-two [obstacles to liberation] — they are to be abandoned because they obstruct attainment (<s>siddhi</s>). || 15 ||
<s>Sūtra</s>: Attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) is eightfold. || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 16 ||

children.text: tadyathā ūhaḥ śabdodhyayanaṃ 3 duḥkhavighātāstrayaḥ 6 suhṛtprāptiḥ 7 dānañca 8 siddhayoṣṭāviti tatropadeśamantareṇa tattvajñānasya svayamūhādyā asiddhiḥ sā prathamā 1 anyadīyaśāstrapāṭhamākarṇya jñānotpattau śabdākhyā dvitīyā 2 adhyayanatastattvajñāne tṛtīyā 3 ādhyātmikādhidaivikādhibhautikaduḥkhatrayavighātena tattvajñāne jāte siddhitrayam 6 jñānavatsuhṛdo lābhena tattvajñāne suhṛtprāptyākhyā saptamī 7 dhanādinārādhite jñānini tattvajñāne 'ṣṭamī 8 atra duḥkhavighātarūpāṇāṃ tisṛṇāṃ siddhīnāṃ mukhyatvamitarāsāṃ tadupāyatvādgauṇatvaṃ bobhyam /
children.translated_text: Namely: reasoning (<s>ūha</s>), verbal [instruction] (<s>śabda</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), three [forms of] removal of suffering (<s>duḥkhavighāta</s>), obtaining a good friend (<s>suhṛtprāpti</s>), and giving (<s>dāna</s>) — these are the eight attainments. Among them, the first attainment is when knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) arises by one's own reasoning without instruction. The second, called '<s>śabda</s>' (verbal), is when knowledge arises from hearing the teaching of another's <s>śāstra</s> (treatise). The third is when <s>tattva</s>-knowledge [comes] through study. When <s>tattva</s>-knowledge arises through the removal of the threefold suffering — <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to oneself), <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to fate/gods), and <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to external beings) — that constitutes three attainments. The seventh, called 'obtaining a good friend,' is when <s>tattva</s>-knowledge [comes] through acquiring a knowledgeable friend. The eighth is when <s>tattva</s>-knowledge [comes through] propitiating a knower [of truth] with wealth and the like. Here it should be understood that the three attainments in the form of removal of suffering are primary, while the others are secondary, being merely means to them.

children.text: pañcaviparyayādārabhyāṣṭasiddhiparyantamete pratyayasargāḥ teṣu prakṛtipratyayānyatākhyātiprepsubhirdvicatvāriṃśadādito heyāḥ siddhayastu upādeyā iti tatsvarūpavyākriyayaiva sūcitaṃ bhavati // 16 //
children.translated_text: From the five errors (<s>viparyaya</s>) through to the eight attainments (<s>siddhi</s>) — these are the intellectual creations (<s>pratyayasarga</s>). Among them, by those who desire the manifestation of the difference between <s>Prakṛti</s> and [the intellectual] dispositions (<s>pratyaya</s>), the forty-two [obstacles] are to be abandoned from the beginning, while the attainments are to be adopted — this is indicated by the very description of their nature. || 16 ||

body.translated_text: Having described the intellectual creation (<s>pratyayasarga</s>), [the author] now states the natural creation (<s>prakṛtisarga</s>).
<s>Sūtra</s>: There are ten fundamental principles (<s>mūlikārtha</s>). || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 17 ||

body.text: daśa arthāḥ padārthāḥ mūlikāḥ santi mūlaṃ prakṛtiḥ puruṣaśca tāvāśrayatvena vidyete yeṣām athavā mūlaṃ svabhāvaḥ sa prayojakatvenāsti yeṣāmiti mūlikā mūlaprakṛtau puruṣe ca vidyamānā iti yāvat tathā ca rājavārttikam /
body.translated_text: There are ten principles (<s>artha</s>), i.e., categories (<s>padārtha</s>), that are fundamental (<s>mūlika</s>). The root (<s>mūla</s>) is <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — these exist as the substratum [of all]. Or alternatively, the root (<s>mūla</s>) means their essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), which exists as the impelling [cause] for those [principles]. 'Fundamental' means existing in the root <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. And thus [states] the <s>Rājavārttika</s>:

children.text: pradhānāstitvamekatvamarthavattvamathānyatā /
children.translated_text: The existence of the Pradhāna (primary substance), its oneness, its purposefulness, and [its] otherness,

children.text: pārārthyaṃ ca tathā naikyaṃ viyogo yoga eva ca //
children.translated_text: its serving another's purpose (<s>pārārthya</s>), and likewise non-unity, separation (<s>viyoga</s>), and conjunction (<s>yoga</s>),

body.translated_text: the functioning of the remainder, and non-agency (<s>akartṛtva</s>) — these are remembered as the ten fundamental principles.

children.text: atraikatvamarthavattvaṃ pārārthyaṃ pradhāne anyatvaṃ prakṛtyapekṣayā akartṛtvaṃ bahutvaṃ puruṣe astitvaṃ yogo viyogaścobhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Here: oneness, purposefulness, and serving another's purpose [pertain to] the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primary substance); otherness (relative to <s>Prakṛti</s>), non-agency, and multiplicity [pertain to] <s>Puruṣa</s>; existence, conjunction (<s>yoga</s>), and separation (<s>viyoga</s>) [pertain to] both.

children.text: śeṣavṛttiḥ aṅgāṅgibhāvena guṇānāṃ vṛttiḥ sthūlasūkṣmaśarīrayoriti /
children.translated_text: The functioning of the remainder (<s>śeṣavṛtti</s>) is the functioning of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) in the relation of principal and subsidiary, in the gross and subtle bodies.

children.text: atra prakṛtipuruṣayoḥ sādharmyavaidharmyanirūpaṇena dvayoḥ pārthakyena jñānaṃ prakṛtipuruṣānyatākhyātibījamiti sūcitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Here, through the determination of the similarities and dissimilarities of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, the knowledge of both as distinct is indicated as the seed of the manifestation of the difference between <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>prakṛtipuruṣānyatākhyāti</s>).

children.text: tathā caiteṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tattatsvabhāvabhūtatvena prakṛtisargatāvyavahāra iti // 17 //
children.translated_text: And thus, because these properties (<s>dharma</s>) have the nature of their respective essences (<s>svabhāva</s>), the designation 'natural creation' (<s>prakṛtisarga</s>) [is applied to them]. || 17 ||

body.text: nanu buddhyādibhireva triguṇātmakaiḥ sakalakāryasiddhau kimadhikaprakṛtyaṅgīkāreṇa ata āha /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Since the complete accomplishment of all effects is possible through <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest — which are of the nature of the three <s>guṇas</s> — what is the need for additionally accepting <s>Prakṛti</s>? To this [the author] replies:
<s>Sūtra</s>: [There is also] the creation through grace (<s>anugrahasarga</s>). || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 18 ||

children.text: buddhyādibhiḥ svakārye 'haṅkārādau janayitavye prakṛteranugrahasahāyopekṣyate anyathā buddhiḥ kṣīṇā satī nālamahaṅkāraṃ janayitumiti sakalopi sargastadanugrahamūlaka evetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest need to produce their own effects — <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) and so on — the grace and assistance of <s>Prakṛti</s> is required. Otherwise, <s>Buddhi</s>, being depleted, would not be capable of producing <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>. Thus the entire creation is rooted in her grace — this is the meaning.

children.text: ayameva prakṛtyāpūra ityucyate tathā ca prakṛtyaivāyaṃ sargo neśvareṇa nāpi brahmopādāno nāpyakāraṇo neśvarādhiṣṭhitaprakṛtita iti sūcyate // 18 //
children.translated_text: This itself is called the 'replenishment by <s>Prakṛti</s>' (<s>prakṛtyāpūra</s>). And thus it is indicated that this creation is by <s>Prakṛti</s> alone — not by <s>Īśvara</s> (a Lord), nor is <s>Brahman</s> its material cause, nor is it without a cause, nor is it from <s>Prakṛti</s> supervised by <s>Īśvara</s>. || 18 ||

body.translated_text: [The author] now states the creation of the subtle elements (<s>tanmātrasarga</s>).
<s>Sūtra</s>: The elemental creation (<s>bhūtasarga</s>) is of fourteen kinds. || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 19 ||

children.text: devatairyagyonamānuṣyabhedena bhūtasargaścaturdaśaprakārako bhavati /
children.translated_text: The creation of beings (<s>bhūtasarga</s>) is of fourteen kinds, divided into [those of] gods, animals, and humans.

children.text: taccettham brāhmaprājāpatyaindrapaitragāndharvayākṣarākṣasapaiśācabhedenāṣṭavidho daivaḥ paśumṛgapakṣisthāvarasarīsṛpabhedena pañcavidhastairyagyona ekavidho mānuṣya iti // 19 //
children.translated_text: That is as follows: the divine [creation] is eightfold, divided into <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Aindra</s>, <s>Paitrya</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Yākṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s>. The animal [creation] is fivefold, divided into domestic animals (<s>paśu</s>), wild animals (<s>mṛga</s>), birds (<s>pakṣi</s>), stationary beings (<s>sthāvara</s>), and reptiles (<s>sarīsṛpa</s>). And the human is of one kind. // 19 //

body.text: nanu puruṣārthaśiromaṇībhūtamokṣatattvākāṅkṣā sati bandhasvarūpajñāna evopapadyate 'to bandhānevāha /
body.translated_text: Now, when there is the desire for the truth of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is the crown jewel of the aims of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), the knowledge of the nature of bondage alone is appropriate. Therefore, [the <s>sūtra</s>] speaks of bondage itself:
<s>Sūtra</s> 20: Bondage is threefold. //

children.text: viparyayādatattvajñānājjāyamāno bandhastrividhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Bondage, arising from error — from non-knowledge of the truth — is threefold:

children.text: prākṛto vaikṛto dākṣiṇaśceti /
children.translated_text: It is <s>prākṛta</s> (relating to <s>Prakṛti</s>), <s>vaikṛta</s> (relating to the evolutes), and <s>dākṣiṇa</s> (relating to [ritualistic] merit).

children.text: tatra puruṣadhiyā prakṛtyupāsanaṃ prākṛto bandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among these, worshipping <s>Prakṛti</s> with the idea that it is <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self) — this is <s>prākṛta</s> (natural) bondage.

children.text: tathā bhūtendriyāhaṅkārabuddhyupāsanaṃ vaikṛtaḥ puruṣatattvamajānataḥ kevalamiṣṭāpūrtakāriṇo dākṣiṇa iti trayāṇāmiti puruṣasvarūpavedakatvābhāve bandhakatvam // 20 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, worshipping the elements (<s>bhūta</s>), sense-organs (<s>indriya</s>), ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), and intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) [as the self] is <s>vaikṛta</s> (modificatory [bondage]). For one who does not know the truth of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self) and merely performs <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (meritorious ritual and charitable works), [this is] <s>dākṣiṇa</s> [bondage]. Thus the bondage of [all] three consists in the absence of the capacity to know the true nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>. // 20 //

body.translated_text: Now, [one asks:] when this threefold ignorance ceases, what kind of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) arises? To this [the <s>sūtra</s>] says:
<s>Sūtra</s> 21: Liberation is threefold. //

children.text: iṣṭāpūrtādikarmasvasāratāṃ puruṣasvarūpopalabdhereva sāratāṃ buddhyamānasya prathamaḥ tato bhūtendriyādiṣvapi vikāratāṃ tataḥ pṛthagātmānaṃ jānataḥ prakṛtirūpastṛtīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who understands the essence of <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> and other ritual actions to be [merely] secondary, and the realization of the true nature of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self) alone to be essential — the first [liberation]. Then, for one who also knows the evolutes such as elements and sense-organs to be mere modifications, and [knows] the self as distinct from them — the third [liberation] is of the nature of <s>Prakṛti</s>.

children.text: yadyapi prathamadvitīyau na tāttvikamokṣau tathāpyaikadeśikānyatākhyatyā tāvadbandhāpagamena mokṣatvavyavahāra iti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Although the first and second are not ultimate (<s>tāttvika</s>) liberation, nevertheless, due to the partial removal of the misidentification [of self with non-self], the convention of calling them 'liberation' insofar as there is the cessation of that [partial] bondage — this should be understood.

children.text: atra bandhamokṣasaṃsārāḥ prakṛtāveva na puruṣe savāsanakleśakarmāśayānāmapariṇāmini puruṣe 'sambhavāt tathā ca bhṛtyajayaparājayayoḥ svāminyupacārāt prakṛtigatānāṃ bandhādīnāṃ puruṣe upacāra eva bhogāpavargayoḥ prakṛtigatayorapi vivekāgrahāt puruṣasambandhaḥ susādhito bhavati /
children.translated_text: Here, bondage, liberation, and <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) belong to <s>Prakṛti</s> alone, not to <s>Puruṣa</s> — because afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) along with their latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), actions (<s>karma</s>), and their residual traces (<s>āśaya</s>) are impossible in <s>Puruṣa</s>, which is unchanging. And just as the victory and defeat of servants are figuratively attributed to the master, so too bondage and the like belonging to <s>Prakṛti</s> are merely figuratively attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>. The connection of <s>Puruṣa</s> with experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), though these belong to <s>Prakṛti</s>, is well established due to the failure to grasp [their] discrimination.

children.text: evaṃ ca dharmajñānājñānavairāgyāvairāgyaiśvaryānaiśvaryaiḥ saptabhī rūpaiḥ prakṛtirbhogāpavargarūpapuruṣārthaṃ pratyātmānaṃ badhnāti tattvajñānena vivekakhyātyā ekena rūpeṇa vimocayati itīdṛśasya tattvajñānasyābhyāsādādaranairantaryadīrghakālasevitāt sattvapuruṣānyatāsākṣātkāri kevalaṃ jñānamutpadyate tenānādirapi viparyayavāsanā pratibadhyate tataścādhyavasāyābhimānasaṅkalpālocanāni antarāṇi bāhyāśca sarve vyāpārā ātmani pratiṣiddhā bhavanti ayameva mokṣa iti siddhāntaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: And thus, <s>Prakṛti</s>, through seven forms — <s>dharma</s> (virtue), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>), non-detachment (<s>avairāgya</s>), mastery (<s>aiśvarya</s>), and non-mastery (<s>anaiśvarya</s>) — binds each self for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s ends, which have the form of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>); and through discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>), which is <s>tattva-jñāna</s> (knowledge of the truth), with a single form, it liberates. From the sustained practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) of such knowledge of the truth — practiced with earnestness, without interruption, and over a long period — there arises pure (<s>kevala</s>) knowledge that directly realizes the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. By that [knowledge], the latent impressions of error (<s>viparyayavāsanā</s>), though beginningless, are obstructed. Then determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), self-assertion (<s>abhimāna</s>), intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), [and] perception (<s>ālocana</s>) — the internal [operations] — and all external activities are negated with respect to the self. This alone is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — this is the established doctrine. // 21 //

body.text: nanu puruṣaprakṛtyādīnāmalakṣyāṇāṃ lakṣyāṇāṃ ca ghaṭapaṭādīnāmakhilaprameyāṇāṃ laukikaiḥ kathamanubhavo vidheyo 'ta āha /
body.translated_text: Now, how can ordinary people have cognition of all knowable objects — both the imperceptible ones like <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, and the like, and the perceptible ones like pots, cloths, and the like? To this [the <s>sūtra</s>] says:
<s>Sūtra</s> 22: The means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is threefold. //

body.text:
asandigdhāviparītānadhigataviṣayā cittavṛttirbodhaśca pauruṣeyaḥ phalaṃ pramā tasyāḥ karaṇaṃ pramāṇam /
tat trividhaṃ pratyakṣānumānaśabdabhedāt /
etenādhikānyupamānādīni naiyāyikādyabhyupagatāni pramāṇāni eṣvevāntarbhavantīti nātiriktānyupayujyante /

children.text: tatrārthasannikṛṣṭamindriyaṃ pratyakṣam /
children.translated_text: Among these, perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is the sense-organ in contact with the object.

children.text: vyāpyavyāpakabhāvapakṣadharmatājñānapūrvakamanumānam /
children.translated_text: Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is [cognition] preceded by the knowledge of the pervaded-pervader relation (<s>vyāpyavyāpakabhāva</s>) and the property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>).

children.text: āptavacanādvedādirūpācchabdamiti /
children.translated_text: Verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is from the statement of a trustworthy person (<s>āptavacana</s>), having the form of the <s>Vedas</s> and the like.

children.text: viśeṣata eṣāṃ lakṣaṇodāharaṇānyākarādavaseyānīti śivam // 22 //
children.translated_text: The specific definitions and examples of these are to be learned from the detailed treatises (<s>ākara</s>). May there be auspiciousness. // 22 //

body.translated_text: A mental modification (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) and cognition that has as its object what is not doubtful, not erroneous, and not previously known — belonging to a person — the result is valid knowledge (<s>pramā</s>). Its instrument is the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). It is threefold, divided into perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). By this, the additional means of knowledge such as analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) and others accepted by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others are subsumed within these [three] alone and thus no additional [means] need be employed.

children.text: ekasmiṃstriguṇātmatattvayutito jātā dvidhā sāpyato dvitvaṃ prāpya prakāśayatyavirataṃ bhogāpavargau svataḥ /
children.translated_text: From the one [<s>Prakṛti</s>] endowed with the nature of the three <s>guṇas</s>, [there] arose the [first] principle (<s>tattva</s>); and from that too, having attained duality, it ceaselessly illuminates both experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) by itself.

children.text: ityevaṃ parisūcayan matimatāṃ mohāpahaṃ kāpilaṃ sūtrāṇāmamalaṃ dvikadvayamidaṃ jīyācciraṃ cetasi //
children.translated_text: Thus, indicating [the teaching] to the wise, may this pure pair of pairs of <s>sūtras</s> of the <s>Kāpila</s> [system], which removes delusion, long live in the mind!

body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sarvopakāriṇī</s>, a concise commentary on the <s>Kāpila Sūtras</s>, is concluded. //
